why: The three export shapes the second review pass broke, each a true edge it dropped: an alias naming a declared object literal (`const api = {find, create}; module.exports = api`), a declared class that is `module.exports` (`module.exports = Base`, then `extends Base` — the canonical CommonJS inheritance shape), and an `Object.assign` export this pass cannot read and so must not enforce. Plus a callback parameter `svc` shadowing the module binding over the callback only: inside, `svc.save()` names whatever was handed in; after it, `svc.find()` is the module's again. `save` is really exported, so only the scope rule — not the export map, not the existence check — can refuse the shadowed call.

refusals.why: PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING. `svc` inside the callback is the callback's parameter. A binding scoped from its start to the end of the enclosing function — pass 2's rule — also swallowed the true `svc.find()` after it; one scoped to the callback refuses only this.

excluded: `merged` is built by `Object.assign`, whose members this pass does not read, so its export map is not enforced: `merged.merge()` is resolved by name and kept because `ts:merged.merge` exists. The call is true — `merge` is on the assigned object.
